title: 5 Easy Ways to Prep Herbs for DIY Salsa Verde at Home
meta_description: Discover five simple methods to prep herbs for salsa verde at home, including tips on using Herb Scissors for fast, uniform chopping.
html:
Making salsa verde from scratch starts with fresh herbs, but the prep can be a bottleneck. Below are five easy ways to prep herbs for salsa verde that keep the flavor bright and the workflow smooth. Whether you’re using a sharp knife, a food processor, or the handy Herb Scissors, these techniques will help you get the perfect texture every time.

1. Quick Rinse and Dry

Before you even think about cutting, give your cilantro, chives, and basil a quick rinse under cold water. Use a salad spinner or gently pat the leaves dry with a clean kitchen towel. Removing excess moisture prevents soggy salsa and makes the herbs easier to handle. If you’re short on time, a single spin in the salad spinner is usually enough to get rid of surface water.

2. Stack, Roll, and Slice

For cilantro and basil, the classic stack‑roll‑slice method works wonders. Gather a handful of leaves, stack them tightly, and roll them into a tight cylinder. Slice the roll cross‑wise with a sharp chef’s knife to produce fine ribbons. This technique yields a consistent size that blends well without over‑processing the herbs.

3. Use a Food Processor for Bulk Prep

If you’re making a large batch of salsa verde, a food processor can save you minutes. Add the rinsed herbs, a splash of lime juice, and a drizzle of olive oil to the bowl. Pulse 3–4 times until the herbs are coarsely minced. Be careful not to over‑process; you want the herbs to retain a bit of texture, not become a puree.

4. Herb Scissors: The One‑Snip Solution

Enter the Herb Scissors. These five‑blade shears are designed to mince cilantro, chives, and basil in a single snip, delivering uniformly chopped herbs without the need for a knife or processor. To use them, simply place a small bunch of herbs between the blades and close the scissors. The built‑in cleaning comb makes removal of stray bits a breeze, so you can keep the workflow moving.

  • Place herbs in the scissors’ jaws.
  • Close the blades—five cuts happen at once.
  • Shake the minced herbs into your bowl and use the comb to clear any leftovers.

The result is a quick, consistent chop that’s perfect for salsa verde, especially when you’re short on prep time.

5. Store Pre‑Chopped Herbs Properly

If you like to have herbs ready for impromptu salsa sessions, store your chopped herbs in an airtight container with a damp paper towel on top. This maintains moisture without making the herbs soggy. For cilantro and basil, a container with a shallow water layer at the bottom (just enough to keep the towel moist) works well. Chopped herbs will stay vibrant for up to two days, giving you instant access for that next salsa verde batch.

Putting It All Together

Once your herbs are prepped, combine them with tomatillos, jalapeños, garlic, and a squeeze of lime. Blend everything together—either in a blender for a smooth texture or by hand for a chunkier feel. The key is that the herbs you’ve prepared using any of the methods above will blend evenly, delivering the fresh, herbaceous punch that defines a great salsa verde.

FAQ

Can I use frozen herbs for salsa verde?

Frozen herbs can be thawed and used, but they lose their bright texture and may introduce excess water. Fresh herbs, prepared with the methods above, give the best flavor and consistency.

Do Herb Scissors work with other herbs like parsley or dill?

Yes, the Herb Scissors handle most leafy herbs. The five‑blade design is especially effective with softer leaves like parsley, dill, and even mint.

How long can I keep pre‑chopped herbs in the fridge?

When stored in an airtight container with a damp paper towel, chopped cilantro, chives, or basil stay fresh for 1–2 days. For longer storage, freeze the chopped herbs in ice‑cube trays with a little water or oil, then transfer to a zip‑top bag.
